title: Parachute fallback policy and acceptance checklist for hosted endpoint lanes (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank)
creator: Sana Patel
summary: Define and validate a 'parachute' fallback policy for hosted inference lanes (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank) that preserves availability and bounded latency during partial degradations. Produce an operational acceptance checklist and launch playbook for canary -> gradual rollout -> full launch.
description:
Problem: Hosted endpoints can experience resource pressure (GPU starvation, degraded kernels, model OOMs, transient infra flaps) leading to increased errors or tail latency. We need a predictable fallback strategy that preserves user-facing availability and provides clear acceptance criteria for launch.

This PRD specifies behavioral requirements, fallback mapping, routing rules, throttles/hedging, monitoring, and the verification checklist required for go/no-go. It focuses on the hosted surface (public API) and the control-plane + serving runtime interactions required to perform automated fallbacks without data loss or inconsistent responses.
scope: Define fallback taxonomy (graceful degrade, variant fallback, region fallback, capacity-tier fallback)
Behavioral mapping for each lane: chat, completions, embeddings, rerank
Runtime API-level fallback triggers: error codes, latency thresholds, queue depths, OOM events
Canary and phased rollout checklist for fallback logic and policy enabling
Integration test harness for synthetic failure injection (kernel hang, GPU OOM, loss of KV cache)
Observability dashboards and alerting rules specific to fallbacks
out_of_scope: Dedicated/Private deployment feature parity (will be addressed in a follow-up PM ticket)
Model selection algorithm research for quality-aware fallback (research to follow)
New billing changes for degraded outputs
acceptance_criteria: When primary model group returns transient 5xx or queue-depth exceeds threshold, system transparently routes to fallback variant within 200ms without returning 5xx to the caller

Fallback responses must satisfy lane-specific quality bounds: embeddings cosine drift < 0.05 vs baseline median; rerank NDCG drop < 0.03; completions semantic similarity > 0.9 on sentinel prompts; chat turn-level coherency checks pass synthetic evals
End-to-end p95 latency under fallback path must be < 800ms for chat and completions for 95% of synthetic traffic profiles
Canary release at 1% traffic shows no more than 1.0% customer-visible errors and no more than 5% change in cost per 1000 tokens compared to baseline
Automated rollback triggers defined and validated (error rate spike > 2x baseline or latency p95 > 2x baseline for 5 minutes) and tested in canary
Operational runbook exists: how to disable fallback policy, diagnosis steps, and postmortem templates
Telemetry hooked: fallback_count, fallback_reason, recovery_time, fallback_success_rate; these are displayed on Console per-route dashboard
End-to-end tests (CI) simulate three failure modes and assert graceful fallback without data corruption
Security/Privacy: fallback preserves data residency policy (requests from EU must not be routed to non-EU-only model variants)
fallback_mapping: Chat: primary=gpt-like-large ; fallback=chat-medium-quantized (lower token throughput but compatible semantics)
Embeddings: primary=embed-astar-1024 ; fallback=embed-compact-512 with deterministic post-normalization to preserve nearest-neighbor stability
Rerank: primary=rnk-large ; fallback=rnk-small-sparse-features + feature-fallback estimated score calibration
triggers_and_thresholds: HTTP 5xx burst of >= 5 requests within 10s for a single node -> mark node degraded
Queue depth per replica > 200 for 30s -> trigger immediate routing to fallback lane for new requests
KV cache miss storm (cache hit ratio drop > 30% over 60s) -> enable cached-prefix mode and fallback for long-context requests
GPU OOM event -> immediate replica drain and traffic migration to fallback variants
Regional capacity shortage -> route to regional fallback with data residency checks
decisions: Use deterministic, lane-specific fallback mappings rather than per-request model selection to keep behavioral guarantees auditable
Fallback logic will live in routing layer (smart router) with a small, versioned policy artifact checked into infra repo
Do not surface fallback to end-users in 1.0; only surface via telemetry and per-request headers for partners during canary
Canary progression: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with automated metric gates
tradeoffs: Quality vs availability: fallback prioritizes availability and bounded latency, accepting small controlled quality regressions
Cost: fallback to cheaper variants may increase token count (e.g., longer prompts for smaller models); acceptance criteria include cost delta limits
Complexity: centralized routing policy increases surface area but reduces per-service duplication
rollout_checklist: Create policy artifact and version it in infra repo
Implement routing hooks in smart-router and smoke test locally
Unit + integration tests for each trigger scenario (GPU OOM, queue surge, cache storm)
End-to-end canary on staging using production-like traffic replay
Execute canary: 1% traffic for 24h, evaluate metrics (errors, p95 latency, fallback rate, quality sentinels)
If canary green, progress to 5% for 48h with same gates; repeat for 20%
Run synthetic chaos test injecting OOMs and kernel stalls while observing rollback behavior
Update Console dashboards and create a dedicated fallback view per route
Run customer-impact review with Solutions Engineering for top 20 customers
Book launch window and on-call rotation for 72h post 100% rollout
qa_plan: Synthetic harness to generate lane-specific sentinel prompts and assert semantic similarity thresholds
Load tests at 1.5x projected peak QPS with controlled node degradation to validate route migration
Chaos engineering play: GPU OOM, kernel timeout, network partition of a region
Regression tests for embeddings nearest-neighbor stability using benchmark dataset
Manual verification: run 50 customer-like queries with and without fallback and produce side-by-side quality diff report
monitoring_and_alerts: Dashboards: fallback rate by lane, fallback_reason histogram, latency p50/p95/p99 split by primary vs fallback
Alerts: fallback_rate > 5% sustained for 10m -> P1 alert; sudden spike in fallback_reasons -> P0
Runbook link attached to alerts with triage steps and immediate rollback action
SLOs updated: availability SLO includes fallback under allowed degradations and measurement method is documented

risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Fallback leads to unacceptable quality regressions for small subset of customers -> Mitigation: per-customer bypass flag and partner notification during canary
Risk: Routing policy misconfiguration routes EU data to non-EU model variants -> Mitigation: policy validation step in CI that enforces residency labels
Risk: Cost increase from fallback usage -> Mitigation: include cost delta gate during canary and throttle fallback if cost delta exceeds threshold
Risk: Observability gaps -> Mitigation: pre-launch checklist requires telemetry coverage and alerting tests
